access_failures.note: Headline and deck were visible, but the article body and precise publication timestamp were inaccessible without a subscription; no source-item record was created.

artifact_policy.note: No article text, images, videos, or binaries were downloaded or committed.

coverage_gaps: No clearly dated primary formal correction or retraction notice concerning Russia-Ukraine war reporting was found in the exact 24-hour window on the queried fact-check and corrections pages.
Search indexing did not resolve direct official URLs for the August 4 Turkish Foreign Ministry statement or the cited Ukrainian social-media posts.
Telegram, X, and other platform-native items were not directly collected where a stable public canonical URL and precise metadata could not be verified.
This was a bounded public-web scan, not an exhaustive search of all outlets, languages, or platforms.
duplicate_or_lineage_notes: The Reuters and AP Black Sea safety reports appear to derive the Turkish reaction from the same Foreign Ministry statement and are not independent evidence of that reaction.
The Guardian briefing is downstream of an Evropeiska Pravda report and should not be counted as an independent primary record of Zaluzhnyi's remarks.
The Reuters Kherson article aggregates several primary social-media and official-video items that require separate source registration before extraction.

excluded_results.reason: Published after the task window ended at 2026-08-04T18:00:00Z. The article contains a clarification that an initial apartment-fire report proved inaccurate, but it was not admitted into the bounded result set.
